history: Chengdu has some 4,500 years of urban civilization — the heart of ancient Shu culture, its symbol the Golden Sun Bird of Jinsha. Qin-era Zhang Yi built the walls; Han brocade gave it the name 'Brocade City', and hibiscus plantings named it 'Hibiscus City'. The Dujiangyan irrigation works made it the 'Land of Abundance'. In 2,300+ years the city has never changed its name or site — unique in China. The Shu kingdom of the Three Kingdoms had its capital here. Today Chengdu is western China's tech, trade and finance hub, a UNESCO City of Gastronomy, famous worldwide for teahouses and pandas.
importance: Capital of Sichuan · First batch National Historical City · Home of the giant panda
unis: Grown from Sichuan Chinese-Western School — the oldest comprehensive university in southwest China.
Founded by merging telecom engineering departments; top in China for electronic information.
From Shanhaiguan Beiyang Railway School — the birthplace of Chinese civil and transport engineering education.
Started as Guanghua University in Shanghai; a leading finance school, called 'the talent pool of Chinese finance'.
A key provincial normal university — the cradle of basic-education teachers in Sichuan.
Born in geology and energy; famous for its national lab on geological disaster prevention.
A family of many ethnic groups studying together, known for ethnic studies.
One of the first four TCM colleges of New China.
A provincial key university with engineering at its core and many disciplines in harmony.
Started as an air-force meteorology training unit; strong in weather and IT.
Chengdu's own comprehensive university — the host of the Universiade Village.
The largest higher music school in southwest China.
One of the earliest PE institutes of New China; a center of martial arts and sports medicine.
China's first independent tourism university; its culinary program is nationally known.
Former Chengdu Military Medical School of the Third Military Medical University.
An important base for training Sichuan's basic-education teachers.
A key base for film and media talent in western China.
An independent college based on UESTC — applied electronic information talents.
foods: Red oil bubbling, numbing and spicy — a whole table around one pot. Chengdu's liveliest way to eat.
Numbing, spicy, hot and tender. 'Chen Mapo' created this world-famous dish 150 years ago.
Noodles once carried on a shoulder pole through the streets, with pickled veggies, minced pork and chili oil.
Skewers of all kinds swished in a red-oil pot — you pay by counting the sticks. Chengdu at its most down-to-earth.
Thin-skinned Sichuan wontons, silky and tender, in clear broth or red oil. The old flagship shop is on Chunxi Road.
Pork dumplings in sweet red-oil soy sauce — a century-old taste, salty, sweet and slightly spicy.
Sliced beef and offal in chili oil with crushed peanuts. Named after a couple who sold it from a street stall.
Little round cakes baked in a copper street pan, crispy outside, soft inside. Students' favorite snack.
Sticky-rice balls thrown at the counter with three loud 'bangs' — the farther they fly, the better the maker.
Braised rabbit head, spicy or five-spice. 'Nibbling rabbit heads' is a true Chengdu pleasure.
scenes: A 2,200-year-old irrigation system built by Li Bing, which turned the plain into the 'Land of Abundance'. A World Heritage Site.
Home of the giant pandas — watch cubs climb and tumble. Panda fans from all over the world come here.
The only shrine in China where a ruler and his minister are worshipped together: Liu Bei and Zhuge Liang. A Three-Kingdoms pilgrimage site.
A Qing-dynasty style street beside Wuhou Shrine — lanterns, snacks and a beautiful night view.
The cottage where the poet Du Fu lived in Chengdu. He wrote his famous 'Broad mansions for all' poem here.
Wide Alley, Narrow Alley and Well Alley from the Qing 'Manchu City' — a living fossil of old Chengdu life.
One of the birthplaces of Taoism. 'Qingcheng, the most serene mountain under heaven' — temples hidden in deep woods.
Ruins of the ancient Shu kingdom. The Golden Sun Bird was unearthed here — now the symbol of Chengdu.
Heming Teahouse has served tea for a century. Ear-cleaning, chatting — the most 'Chengdu' afternoon ever.
A Ming-dynasty covered bridge over the Jin River, full of restaurants and bars, glowing like a treasure ship at night.
